assessment: This important study by Ruesseler, Weber and colleagues employs psychophysical kernels and EEG reverse correlation methods to identify the decision process adjustments used to account for variations in target frequency and duration in a task in which targets emerge periodically within a continuous stimulus stream. The paper provides solid evidence for the role of leak and threshold adjustments. The paper will be of interest to researchers studying mathematical models and neurophysiological correlates of decision making and more broadly authors with an interest in the application of reverse correlation techniques for neural signal analysis.
